question: Does one isolated Cirrove Shared Drive mount remain usable and keep its feed ready during a one-hour session of repeated reads of a known run-owned file?
kind: Pre-registered single-arm live duration probe; one run does not establish population reliability or a memory trend
scope: One Workspace administrator, one owned Shared Drive and one previously verified 85-byte test file. No cloud mutation. A fresh private daemon and FUSE mount; the installed daemon and its three mounts stay untouched.
arms: A: sample the private daemon status and read the exact test file through FUSE once per minute for at least 60 minutes; record feed state, mount state, result latency and process RSS
B: after the 60-minute window ends, stop only the recorded private daemon PID and confirm its mount is gone while the installed daemon and its original mounts remain active
endpoint: Pass the bounded duration probe only with at least 61 successful samples spanning 60 minutes, every file hash matching the pre-registered SHA-256, every mount ready with no failed upload or stuck change, each feed success no older than five minutes, and private cleanup completed. On a failure record the first failing sample and preserve private state. RSS values are descriptive only; one arm cannot prove leak freedom.
prediction: The existing read-only path should keep the small file readable while the Shared Drive poll feed stays ready, but token refresh or mount lifetime may reveal a failure outside the earlier short probes.
first_attempt: The private mount appeared, but the harness applied the ready/feed-success gate immediately and stopped before sample zero. Its own mount disappeared and the installed daemon and three mounts were unchanged. This does not answer the one-hour question; the failed manifest is retained.
followup_correction: Allow up to 120 seconds after the mount appears for the initial ready/feed-success observation before starting the one-hour clock. The 61-sample endpoint and all content checks remain unchanged.
temporary_filesystem: findmnt -T for the retry's private TMPDIR and SQLITE_TMPDIR resolved to /home on btrfs, not tmpfs; the actual private paths are recorded in the run manifest.

result.content_and_feed: All 61 numbered samples reported ready and mounted, matched the registered 85-byte file SHA-256, and passed the supervisor's no-save-refusal/no-failed-upload/no-stuck-change gate. Every sampled feed last-success value was fresh; an upper-bound reconstruction from completion time puts the maximum age at 32.3 seconds against the pre-registered 300-second limit.
result.private_cleanup: The supervisor stopped only its recorded private daemon PID; its private FUSE mount disappeared. The installed cirroved service stayed active with PID 2764811 and its original OneDrive, GoogleDrive and Calista mounts unchanged, independently checked after completion.
result.descriptive_resources: Within this single run, sample latency median was 9.492 ms and maximum 11.722 ms; private-daemon VmRSS ranged from 41132 to 42768 KiB, beginning at 41132 and ending at 42768 KiB. The 1636 KiB within-run spread is reported beside that change. One run with a repeatedly read small file cannot establish a memory trend or general provider reliability.
result.limit: The repeated file may have been served from Cirrove's cache after the first read. Fresh feed success exercises ongoing provider metadata access, but this probe does not prove a late uncached content download, a restricted-role account or a 24-hour session.
